issues.parameter: orbital period, spin period, and synchronization
issues.competing_evidence: Tovmassian+00 gives spectroscopic Porb=0.14063 d (3.37512 h); candidate range 0.14002–0.14092 d is a searched range, not an uncertainty. Photometric/cyclotron period matches within ~1 min over 1 yr, but paper says absolute synchronism is unproven and interprets the photometric period as WD spin. Harrison & Campbell+15 report sparse/noisy WISE modulation roughly half the binary period and do not plot it. Zengin Çamurdan+23 reports corrected photometric periods but exact V388 Peg value is inaccessible in the publisher preview. TESS sector 55 final period is 202.756±0.010 min but Tmag=17.495±0.060, near the paper’s increasing-unreliability threshold; ACF=202.4000 min, other methods blank.
issues.why_it_matters: Mislabeling a light-curve modulation as orbital or spin changes the inferred synchronization state and evolutionary comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Obtain Zengin Çamurdan+23 full text and inspect the T100 ephemeris/data; retain spectroscopic 3.37512 h orbital value and all distinct photometric periods until resolved. Do not assume synchronization.
issues.public_status: Awaiting access to the original source

issues.parameter: white dwarf magnetic field by emitting region and method
issues.competing_evidence: Tovmassian+00 obtains ~20 MG from a homogeneous one-temperature accretion-plasma cyclotron model (kT~20 keV, θ~80°, logΛ~5.7; parameters trade off; no resolved harmonics/Zeeman lines). Harrison & Campbell+15 suggest ~25 MG only if WISE W2 humps are cyclotron. Barrett+20 reports 3563±730 G only under n=1 donor-coronal electron-cyclotron-maser assumption.
issues.why_it_matters: The kG radio plasma estimate and MG cyclotron-region model do not measure the same component; treating them as one WD surface field would be physically wrong.
issues.needed_action: Keep three component/method-specific values in the measurement ledger; do not adopt a direct WD photospheric field without a resolved Zeeman/cyclotron diagnostic.

issues.parameter: X-ray flux, bandpass and spectral model
issues.competing_evidence: Tovmassian+00 RASS 0.1–2.4 keV unabsorbed 5.5e-13 erg cm-2 s-1 assumes 40 eV blackbody+20 keV bremsstrahlung from only 24 photons. Zengin Çamurdan+23 preview reports Swift 2014 0.3–10 keV unabsorbed 3.6e-12 for assumed 30 keV bremsstrahlung. Ridder+23 Table 3 compiles 2SXPS/Evans+20 1–10 keV 4.1±0.8e-12 but lists 0.1–10 keV 6±2e-11; the broad-band value is ~15 times the narrower-band value. Epochs, models/conversions and absorption convention differ or are not source-specifically documented.
issues.why_it_matters: The band/model discrepancy affects X-ray-to-radio comparisons and any luminosity/accretion-rate inference.
issues.needed_action: Inspect Zengin full spectral-fit table and Swift observation details; retrieve Evans/2SXPS source product and Ridder conversion; preserve native/model-dependent products separately until reconciled.

issues.competing_evidence: Tovmassian+00 estimates 300–600 pc by assuming an M4/M5 donor and rough Av≈0.37; no direct donor subtype is measured there. Gaia EDR3 Bailer-Jones exact source-ID geometric posterior is 721.052 (+76.735/-54.343) pc; photogeometric alternative 705.117 (+70.836/-57.170) pc. Ridder+23 rounds the geometric-like Gaia distance to 720(+80/-50) pc.
issues.why_it_matters: An assumed donor subtype and old model distance must not be treated as measured donor properties or as a current astrometric distance.
issues.needed_action: Retain Gaia/Bailer-Jones posterior as the catalog astrometric distance; keep Tovmassian’s model-dependent distance as historical context and M4/M5 as assumed, not measured.

references.note: Original ApJ PDF retrieved from public MPE-hosted copy and text-extracted to tmp/pdfs/text/Tovmassian+00_V388Peg.txt. Discovery/follow-up paper for V388 Peg/RX J2157.5+0855: reports Porb=0.14063 d = 3.375 h from radial velocities/light curves, with photometric/cyclotron and spectroscopic/orbital periods agreeing within about 1 min over 1 yr but absolute synchronism not proven. Narrow emission component is attributed to the X-ray/UV-irradiated secondary (gamma~59 km/s, K_NEL~72 km/s; summary K~75 km/s), high-velocity component mainly to the accretion stream. Spectropolarimetry shows circular polarization up to about 15 percent and supports a one-pole cyclotron-beaming geometry with i~45 deg and magnetic colatitude ~45 deg. Cyclotron modeling gives B~20 MG for a simple homogeneous one-temperature accretion plasma (kT=20 keV, polar angle ~80 deg, log Lambda=5.7), but no resolved cyclotron harmonics or Zeeman lines are detected, so the value is approximate/model-dependent. Donor type M4/M5 is assumed from photometric-minimum distance and the period-spectral-type relation; no WD photospheric Teff, WD mass, donor mass, or donor Teff is measured. Full bibliographic metadata cross-checked; original full paper reviewed again for this source checkpoint.
